subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw core own pace-aware provider usage controls for autonomous agents, and should the first accepted phase be observability-only or include enforcement?
rationale: The remaining work would add provider-specific usage semantics, persisted state, new agent config, status/tool output, and autonomous throttling behavior; source inspection can prove the gap but cannot choose that product boundary.

options.title: Phase Observability First
options.body: Capture or derive pace context and expose it in status/session_status without blocking autonomous work until provider semantics and cost models are proven.

options.title: Add Opt-In Enforcement
options.body: Introduce disabled-by-default pace thresholds that can throttle subagents, with explicit config, tests, and operator recovery guidance.

options.title: Plugin/API First
options.body: Keep core lean by designing generic provider and agent hooks so a plugin can own Anthropic-specific pace policy without hardcoding it in core.

recommendation.title: Phase Observability First
recommendation.body: Capture or derive pace context and expose it in status/session_status without blocking autonomous work until provider semantics and cost models are proven.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest product-scoping signal and adjacent provider-quota UI history among the identified people.
